ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier) Articles L.561-1 through L.561-50 (AML/CFT), Article L.562-1 et seq. (EU and UN sanctions implementation), Articles L.561-45 through L.561-46-1 (UBO declaration obligations); French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) Articles L.123-28-1, R.123-220-1 to R.123-220-9 (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs); Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II); Decree No. 2016-1806 of 19 December 2016 (RBE requirement); Decree No. 2018-284 of 18 April 2018; EU Regulation (EU) 2015/847 (wire transfer information); EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843 as transposed; French Order of 2 September 2020 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing for non-financial entities; ACPR and Tracfin instructions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (1961) or Consular Legalization for non-Hague countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy by a notary or French consulate, then Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization where required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against French national (Ministry of Economy and Finance) asset freeze lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions lists, UK OFSI, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions, and domestic French PEP register maintained by Tracfin; Enhanced Due Diligence is required for any PEP, family member, or close associate under Articles L.561-10 and L.561-10-1. Screening frequency: at UBO identification, before incorporation, and on a continuous risk-based basis; does not rely solely on database screening; source of wealth and source of funds must be documented for any PEP or high-risk jurisdiction. The protocol includes a 5-step verification: (1) Verify identity with valid official ID; (2) Sanctions list screening with fuzzy matching; (3) PEP determination; (4) Adverse media check; (5) Risk rating and escalated approval for high-risk DG forwarding activity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) — RNE (Registre National des Entreprises) online portal and the French business formalities website 'formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr'; local clearance via the commercial court registry (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce), and verification via 'Infogreffe'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in Latin-based characters; non-French language names are permitted only if presented in a transliterated or French-compatible Latin script. Under the Loi Toubon (Law 94-665 of 4 August 1994), mandatory French language for official documents and public filing; a French translation must accompany any foreign-language naming declaration. The name must be written in a clear, legible form, and French law requires every trading name to be used consistently; there is no full prohibition of foreign names, but they must not be contrary to public policy or morality.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Société Anonyme (incorporation form token used misleadingly)
KPMG, Deloitte, or other regulated designations implying regulated corporate form
Explosifs / Matières dangereuses (unless prior ministerial authorization obtained)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The rejection notice may be available through the RNE/INPI; the applicant may challenge the name rejection by filing an administrative appeal with the President of the Commercial Court (Tribunal de Commerce) within one month of the refusal, through a formal request (assignation) or via a direct referral per Article L.123-5 Code de commerce; alternatively refile a corrected name. Exact administrative appeals follow Articles R.123-27 Code de commerce and the general administrative appeals against refusal of a declaration. Extension requires re-filing a new valid name with updated documents if the original reservation expires; rejection appeal can be combined with a priority trademark registration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A SAS must have a real registered office (siège social) that can receive official correspondence; a pure virtual office is not per se prohibited for the registered office if domiciliation services are provided by a legal authorized domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) under Articles L.123-11-2 and L.123-11-3 Code de commerce, with a maximum duration of 3 months for new companies? Actually, the duration is contractual but must be compatible with commercial substance; for regulated DG forwarding under ISIC 5229, a virtual office alone will NOT satisfy commercial substance requirements, because an actual operational management location and DG control premises are required for licensing and customs obligations. Documentary virtual office may be acceptable for registered address only, but the physical operating site must be independent and approved; therefore virtual office permissibility is conditional and discouraged.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (70-85% probability over the first 12 months of operation). DG freight forwarders are subject to surprise inspections by DREAL (regional environmental and transport authority), Customs (DGDDI), and the DG transport enforcement unit under the ORSEC/DG regulations; on-site inspection can also occur for RBE and anti-money-laundering audits by Tracfin under a combined inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Book II, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); Code civil Articles 1832 et seq.; Code monétaire et financier for AML/CFT compliance.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: INPI Guichet unique des entreprises and Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) administered by greffes des tribunaux de commerce.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs de la SAS; Déclaration de constitution / formulaire M0 via the Guichet unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for a SAS. Cash shares must be paid up at least 50% at incorporation, with the balance due within five years. Subscribed funds are deposited in a blocked bank or notarial escrow account and released upon RCS registration. Registry/greffe fees and legal announcement costs apply separately.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: First Board Resolution of [COMPANY] SAS. The undersigned directors, duly convened, resolve: (1) approve subscription of [NUMBER] shares at [AMOUNT] per share, fully or partly paid as required, for aggregate capital of [AMOUNT]; (2) adopt the registered office at [ADDRESS] and authorize filing with the RCS; (3) appoint [NAME] as Président and [NAME] as Directeur Général, granting authority to sign filings, open bank accounts, and execute incorporation acts; (4) authorize the Président to publish notices and complete all formalities. Adopted unanimously, effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of statuts; constitutive shareholders' meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders / notaire if non-cash contributions require appraisal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare French-language statuts specifying SAS form, corporate purpose including dangerous goods forwarding, registered office, capital, share rights, governance, and Président. Hold constitutive meeting; sign statuts; appoint first officers; approve registered office. Notarize only if apports en nature require independent appraisal.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office (lease or domiciliation agreement)
Apport en nature appraisal if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registry rejects, amend statuts by unanimous shareholder decision and re-execute; file rectified documents without new publication if changes are non-substantive.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked share capital deposit and attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account in the company name; deposit at least 50% of cash subscriptions; obtain attestation de dépôt de fonds. Keep funds blocked until RCS registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank refuses, use a notarial escrow; if amount insufficient, complete capital and obtain corrected attestation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal announcement in a journal d'annonces légales (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales authorized in the department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a constitution notice within one month of statuts execution containing company name, form, capital, registered office, and RCS city. Obtain dated receipt/proof.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notice contains error, publish a corrective notice; retain both receipts for RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation dossier via INPI Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des entreprises / RCS greffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create account on formalities.inpi.fr; complete formulaire M0; upload statuts, attestation de dépôt de fonds, JAL receipt, domiciliation proof, IDs, and declarations; pay greffe fees; submit electronically.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to INPI query within stated deadline; cure by correcting or uploading missing documents; if rejected, refile M0 with reasoned appeal to greffe.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of Kbis / SIREN/SIRET
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / INSEE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After INPI validation, obtain Kbis extract and SIREN/SIRET. Verify legal identity, capital, officers, and registered office. Use Kbis for bank, licences, and contracts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Kbis data incorrect, request RCS rectification via INPI; if refused, apply to president of tribunal de commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for corporate income tax, VAT, and social contributions; apply for EORI and customs authorizations for DG forwarding; register excise if applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File corrective returns; request online regularization; contest penalties through DGFiP.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of definitive corporate bank account and release of escrow
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Kbis, open operating account; present Kbis, statuts, and beneficial ownership; release blocked capital into account; obtain bank certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank refuses, escalate to Banque de France mediation; use alternative bank; retain proof for compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of corporate governance and shareholder registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold first board meeting; appoint Directeur Général if any and auditor if thresholds met; adopt fiscal year, accounting policies, and registers; file UBO at RCS.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify minutes by subsequent decision; update RCS filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for dangerous goods forwarding and transport authorizations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File for préfectoral DG authorization; appoint certified DGSA; obtain ADR/IMDG/IATA-DGR certifications; provide insurance, security plan, and premises approval.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Complete missing records; appeal silent refusal to administrative court; request reasoned decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: ICPE environmental and civil defense clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File ICPE declaration, enregistrement, or authorization; prepare EIA if required; submit fire safety and structural load studies; obtain SDIS/commission clearance before operation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to incomplete file; resubmit revised studies; appeal préfectoral refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain DAC, safety reports, training, and insurance; undergo periodic inspections; renew authorizations before expiry; update RCS and UBO changes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Implement corrective action plan; contest sanctions via administrative appeal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de la Transition écologique et de la Cohésion des territoires (DGPR/DREAL); DGAC for air transport; DGAMPA for maritime; préfecture for road DG authorizations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation préfectorale d'exercice pour le transport et la manutention de marchandises dangereuses (DG) and Licence de commissionnaire de transport; DGSA certification and modal ADR/IMDG/IATA-DGR approvals.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autorité environnementale (Ae), MRAe and DREAL under Code de l'environnement, with Ministère de la Transition écologique.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: ICPE: Déclaration, Enregistrement, or Autorisation; full EIA Report for Autorisation and cas-par-cas for Enregistrement. DG storage/warehousing commonly falls under rubriques 1510, 1436, or 4331.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with ICPE arrêtés ministériels (e.g., 04/10/2010), IED 2010/75/EU, Water Act, and Air Code; wastewater pH 5.5–8.5, suspended solids, COD, hydrocarbons <5 mg/L, heavy metals; VOC emission limits; waste traceability via Trackdéchets; 100% spill containment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: SDIS/commission de sécurité approval, ICPE fire study, sprinklers, and ATEX zones; structural load inspection; workplace clearance: DREAL/Inspection du travail, DUERP, CSE, and medical surveillance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) acting through the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE), with the professional portal accessible via impots.gouv.fr and the French Customs and Indirect Taxation Directorate (DGDDI) for import/export controls.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity establishing French taxable presence (e.g. through a fixed establishment or a French registered branch of an SAS) must obtain French tax identification through the Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises or the relevant SIE. The procedure comprises: (1) filing the initial registration file (SIREN/SIRET) with INSEE, (2) obtaining the TVA intracommunautaire (French VAT ID) from DGFiP where liable to French VAT, and (3) obtaining a French Customs EORI number from DGDDI for customs and dangerous goods freight forwarding. The registration file must identify the entity’s legal form (Société par Actions Simplifiée), beneficial owner, statutory representation, place of technically effective management (principal establishment in France), and business license for regulated hazardous-material transport.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate United States-style check-the-box election. An SAS is a company taxable at entity level on French corporation tax at the standard 25% rate, including distributed profits subject to the parent-subsidiary regime for qualifying shareholders. Available statutory elections include the election to form a French tax group (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI where a 95% French or EEA parent controls the chain; the election to be subject to the simplified real-tax regime for small and medium companies; and the ATAD anti-hybrid neutralisation mechanism under Articles 205 A et seq. CGI, which applies automatically rather than by elective check-the-box. No pass-through election is available for an SAS.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0.00. France has no de minimis VAT registration exemption for suppliers established or having a fixed establishment in France; every taxable person effecting taxable supplies in the course of an economic activity must register for French VAT from the first euro of taxable turnover. For non-established suppliers supplying B2B freight-forwarding and ancillary dangerous-goods logistics services to French or EU customers, a French VAT ID is required from the first transaction without any turnover threshold. Distance-selling thresholds are replaced by the OECD/EU OSS regime and do not affect the dangerous-goods freight-forwarding business model, which is overwhelmingly B2B.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates progressive domestic e-invoicing from 1 September 2026 for large and intermediate enterprises and from 1 September 2027 for small and very small enterprises, through certified dematerialisation platforms (PDPs) and the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) architecture. Structured electronic data (Factur-X/UBL/CII) and transaction-level e-reporting will be transmitted to DGFiP via the PPF. For export customs clearance, DGDDI requires digital submission of the Single Administrative Document (SAD/DELTA) on the DELTA platform, plus the export summary declaration (EXA/EXE) in ICS and real-time validation of dangerous-goods declarations against regulated classification codes. No French ‘fiscal stamping’ or invoice-level real-time clearance mechanism currently applies, but excise and safety-controlled movements of hazardous chemicals may be subject to EU Excise Movement and Control System controls and submission to French Customs for release of transit/export consignment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (TVA exonérée avec droit à déduction) for exports is available under Article 262-I CGI for goods definitively exported outside the European Union. A qualifying exporter must be able to demonstrate that the goods physically left the EU in their export state. Services ancillary to exported goods, including international freight forwarding, storage of goods in transit, customs brokerage and dangerous-goods transport, may be zero-rated pursuant to Article 259-A 1° CGI when the services are directly related to goods that have been exported and are directly attributable to transport to a destination outside the EU. For B2B services to non-EU recipients not falling within the place-of-supply reverse-charge rules, French VAT will generally not apply. Sufficient contemporaneous shipping, contractual, safety and banking evidence must be maintained for at least the French statutory records retention period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document SAD/DELTA) with export summary declaration (EXA/EXE) filed through French Customs DELTA system
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill evidencing actual physical departure of the dangerous goods from the EU customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/broker substantiation that export proceeds will be repatriated and accounted for within statutory timelines
Commercial invoice and packing list matching HS codes, quantity, gross/net weight and shipping marks

Dangerous goods transport documentation (IMDG/ADR declaration, Material Safety Data Sheet, Transport Emergency Card / TREM card, stowage and segregation certificate) proving compliance with regulated classification rules
Logistics contract, forwarding order and letter of indemnity demonstrating the SAS acted as principal freight forwarder or contractual carrier for the export movement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: French tax and customs authorities may undertake a retrospectivereclassification of zero-rated export transactions where export documentation is missing, contradictory, or fraudulent. The administration may assess the 20% French VAT as due from the exporter, add statutory late-payment interest, and apply penalties under Article 1729 CGI of up to 40% for negligence or up to 80% for serious misstatement or fraudulent conduct. Where the zero-rating claim is part of a systematic abuse using fictitious export documentation, the exporter and its officers may face criminal penalties under Articles 1741 and 1743 CGI, including imprisonment, financial penalties of up to EUR 1,000,000 and personal penalties, together with customs forfeiture sanctions for breach of DGDDI customs regulations. For dangerous-goods forwarders, failure to substantiate valid export may also trigger administrative suspension or withdrawal of the regulated transport licence and joint liability for unpaid excise duties or safety-control penalties under relevant environmental and transport laws.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as banking and payment-institution supervisor, jointly with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) at the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty for cross-border capital movement rules and FX-related authorizations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France, as a euro-area member state, has full convertibility of the euro for both current and capital account transactions in accordance with EU Capital Movements Directive 88/361/EEC and the TFEU free movement of capital provisions. Profit remittances from an SAS can be executed freely after statutory audit and tax compliance, subject to anti-money laundering / counter-terrorist financing (AML/CFT) screening, EU sanctions and restrictive measures, and the ordinary declaration duties set out in the Code monétaire et financier (CMF). No exchange control rationing, repatriation delays, or surrender requirements apply to EUR or freely convertible currencies. Non-EU direct investments, particularly into sectors affecting the transport of dangerous goods or dual-use sensitive supply chains, may trigger ex-ante screening under EU Regulation 2019/452 and the associated French foreign-investment control rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France maintains no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation or mandatory conversion ratio for exporters; proceeds may be retained in EUR or any freely convertible currency. The only formal requirements are (i) accurate submission of export declarations in the customs Single Administrative Document (SAD/EX1) for the physical movement of dangerous goods, (ii) bank-driven reporting to the Banque de France for each cross-border flow exceeding the applicable reporting threshold (EUR 50,000 per operation for statistical balance-of-payments reporting), and (iii) compliance with EU sanctions, export-control licensing, and dual-use regulations for regulated hazardous chemicals or dangerous goods.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational EUR/Multi-currency Account
Operational Account with Trade Finance and FX Hedging

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Treasury and Cross-Border Clearing Account
Multi-currency Operational Account and Documentary Credit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for primary treasury operations. Offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) without a PSD2 license properly passported into France cannot legally provide current accounts, payment services, or e-money issuance to a French-resident SAS. ACPR-licensed or EEA-passported fintech EMIs may offer secondary disbursement accounts, but they are not appropriate as the sole treasury rail for a High-Risk dangerous-goods forwarding entity that requires documentary credits, sanctioned-jurisdiction filtering, and specialist correspondent banking. Conventional tier-1 banks remain mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French banking law and ACPR AML/CFT guidance do not universally require physical presence of all directors for KYC onboarding; remote onboarding using certified e-identification and video verification is legally possible. However, for an ISIC 5229 dangerous-goods transporter classified as High-Risk and requiring a special operating license, French banks will in practice demand: (i) an in-person KYC interview of the legal representatives/general manager at the company’s registered office or at the bank branch, (ii) a bank-site visit or video-site inspection of the operational premises and DG storage/cross-docking facility, (iii) original or certified corporate resolutions, and (iv) certified copy of passports and proof of residence. Non-signatory minority shareholders may be onboarded remotely with valid eIDAS certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Hazardous-goods sector risk: dangerous goods forwarding is automatically classified as a high-risk money-laundering typology requiring enhanced due diligence; absence of specialised DG licences and safety certificates.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (1) current Kbis extract and statutes; (2) hazardous-goods transport licences (ADR for road, IMDG for sea, IATA DGR for air) and Logistics Compliance approval; (3) Dangerous Goods Safety Adviser (DGSA) appointment letter and certificate; (4) ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, and ISO 45001:2018 certificates; (5) environmental and third-party liability insurance coverage; (6) public-liability proof for warehouse/terminal operations; and (7) copies of the Safety Management System (SMS) and incident-response plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership or PEP-associated shareholders: unexplained ownership chains or politically exposed persons in the shareholder register.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (1) the French Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) certified extract; (2) full shareholder ownership chain to natural persons with identity documents; (3) PEP self-declaration and risk explanation; (4) source of wealth and source of funds documentation for each expected capital contribution above EUR 10,000; (5) tax residence certificates for all direct/indirect shareholders; and (6) sworn declaration of no affiliation with arms-trafficking, sanctioned entities, or prohibited chemical trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk cross-border payments: freight-forwarding flows through jurisdictions subject to EU unilateral sanctions, OFAC embargoes, or FATF grey-list status.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit (1) written AML/CFT and sanctions-compliance policy tailored to DG logistics; (2) live sanctioned-party screening and denied-party screening logs with false-positive resolution procedure; (3) full transaction-flow map identifying each counterparty bank, intermediary, and beneficiary; (4) export licences, import certificates, and end-user undertakings for controlled chemicals; (5) original Bills of Lading / air waybills and dangerous-goods declarations (DGD); (6) copies of commercial contracts containing sanctions, cargo-exclusions, and anti-diversion warranties; and (7) relevant records of declarations made to French customs and the Direction Générale du Trésor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unsubstantiated revenue and trade capacity: inability to evidence the scale and legitimacy of freight operations, supply-chain cycle times, and logistics stock levels.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (1) statutory auditor’s report (rapport du commissaire aux comptes), if appointed, covering the last two financial years; (2) audited or reviewed financial statements; (3) management accounts and aged AP/AR ledgers; (4) 12-month cash-flow forecast; (5) signed logistics contracts with three major clients/shippers; (6) sample export/import declarations (SAD, EX1/IM4); (7) customs broker and consignee mandate letters; and (8) a completed bank-specific KYC business questionnaire (fCOI/AML) confirming expected transaction volumes, counterparty jurisdictions, aggregate annual turnover, and purpose of each active relationship.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound non-resident capital contributions to the French SAS must be wired over SWIFT using MT103 for third-party transfers or MT202 for nostro/vostro interbank movements. The instructing bank must include a transparent human-readable purpose code in field 72: 'CAPITAL INCREASE' or 'APPORT EN COMPTE COURANT'; for balance-of-payments classification the EU ROC code used by French banks is typically 'B.7.1' or 'C.3.1' for direct-investment equity, and 'C.2.1' for shareholder loans, while custom references should state the notarial/social resolution date and capital-increase amount. The receiving French bank will require the shareholder resolution, proof of source of funds, and for any non-EU direct investment above EUR 1.5 million the mandatory ex-ante or short ex-post statistical declaration to the Banque de France using its Inbound Foreign Direct Investment reporting portal. If an escrow account is used for SAS formation, release to the operational account is permitted only after the deposit of the capital (blocage du capital) is lifted by the Caisse des Dépôts or legal depositary, and after registration of the SAS on the RNE.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For international trade settlements France uses TARGET2 for intra-EU EUR corridors and the SWIFT network for global wires. Generic outbound cargo payments and freight disbursements are executed using SWIFT MT103 with full beneficiary details and the relevant EU ROC purpose code 'C.2.4' (trade credit) or 'C.1.1' (services). Commercial documentary credits are issued through password-authenticated SWIFT MT700 conforming to ICC UCP600; for dangerous-goods transport, transport documents (airway bill, Bill of Lading, and Dangerous Goods Declaration) must be exact in description, quantity, UN number, and packing group. Outbound payments are systemically screened against EU Regulation 833/2014, OFAC and UN sanctions lists, and the French Financial Action Task Force expectations; any payment or documentary credit above the Banque de France balance-of-payments threshold (EUR 50,000 individually or EUR 250,000 annual aggregated for treasury purposes) must be declared by the bank or treasury department to the Banque de France via the online statutory reporting portal.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable plain-vanilla EUR/USD FX forward customised to DG contract invoicing calendar
FX swap (dévise contre devise) for rolling unwinding of foreign-currency receivables/payables
Cross-currency swap for hedging income/expense mismatches on multi-currency logistics funding
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) in restricted-convertibility currencies (e.g. INR, KRW, PHP) permitted as an OTC derivative under EMIR with mandatory clearing and margin fulfilment where applicable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of result
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAS shareholders or sole shareholder; no routine filing authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after financial year-end, unless a court-authorized extension applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential court order to convene the shareholders and personal liability for directors where statutory duties are breached; no automatic strike-off solely for missing the approval deadline

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce), through the relevant filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A fine of up to EUR 1,500, or EUR 3,000 for repeat offending; the president of the commercial court may order filing, potentially subject to a daily coercive penalty. No automatic strike-off deadline applies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French tax authority (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after financial year-end; for a calendar-year taxpayer, generally the second working day after 1 May, subject to the annual electronic filing schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge generally starts at 10% and may rise to 40% after formal notice or 80% in specified cases, plus late-payment interest; no automatic corporate strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French tax authority (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the 15th day of the fourth month after financial year-end; for a calendar-year taxpayer, 15 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest generally accrues at 0.20% per month, with applicable tax surcharges; no automatic corporate strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally required if the SAS exceeds at least two of these thresholds at financial year-end: EUR 5 million total assets, EUR 10 million net turnover, or 50 average employees. Separate requirements apply to certain groups, controlled entities, and regulated activities. Dangerous-goods forwarding alone does not establish an audit exemption or an additional audit threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French accounting standards (Plan comptable général) for individual statutory accounts; IFRS is generally relevant to consolidated accounts where required or elected under applicable rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France has no general annual UBO confirmation filing. Review UBO information annually as a compliance control and file an update with the commercial court registry within 30 days of a change. Changes to share ownership must also be recorded in the applicable share-transfer records and reported as required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholder account records and share-transfer movement records)
Register of Directors and corporate officers
Minute Book or records of shareholder decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 150-600 per year (approximately USD 165-660), depending on location and service scope
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 3,000-10,000 per year (approximately USD 3,300-11,000); scope, group status, and business complexity materially affect fees

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard French corporate income tax rate for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2022; qualifying SMEs pay 15% on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit and 25% on the remainder)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% on eligible R&D expenses up to EUR 100,000,000 and 5% above; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) for SMEs; patent-box reduced rate of 10% for eligible licensed IP; accelerated depreciation for green and digital investments
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward; annual offset capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the excess taxable profit for losses arising in fiscal years closing on or after 1 January 2015

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Liasse fiscale (Form 2065-SD and annexes 2050-2058 series), filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr or certified EDI/EDI-TDFC tax software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (accompanied by four quarterly prepayment instalments of estimated CIT and one final balance payment after the annual return)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year SAS: e-filing due by 3 May (or the next business day) of the following year. For non-calendar fiscal years: within three months of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN/SIRET, APE/NAF code (5229Z for dangerous goods freight), registered office address, tax regime and fiscal year open/close dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact French-issued SIREN; state the French head-office address regardless of non-resident management board seats.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B/C: Shareholding and beneficial ownership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of direct and indirect shareholders, percentage of capital and voting rights, and full chain of beneficial owners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all non-resident corporate and individual shareholders; attach evidence of tax residence for any treaty or EU directive claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit/loss before tax, used as the starting point of the tax computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No special adjustment should be made merely because the SAS is non-resident owned; the French entity is taxed as a standalone French resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible charges (e.g. excessive management fees, hidden profit distributions) and deductible business expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident parent invoices charges or royalties, ensure full transfer-pricing support exists and that each charge is arm's length, evidenced and beneficial.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of tax losses carried forward and current-year deductible amount after the statutory cap
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the unlimited but capped carryforward rule; keep ownership-continuity records if the foreign holding percentage changed during the period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of French tax credits (CIR, CII, foreign tax credits) to reduce corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax credits are computed at the SAS level; non-resident shareholders cannot appropriate French tax credits attached to distributed profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Return of intercompany payments, receipts, and pricing methodology if related-party transactions exceed statutory thresholds
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident parent must cooperate in obtaining group data; failure to file Form 2257 when triggered exposes the SAS to a 5% penalty on the sums concerned.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing first triggers late-payment interest at 0.20% per month plus a 10% penalty on the CIT due. After formal notice, the penalty increases to 40%, or 80% if confidential undisclosed activity is later uncovered. In addition, omission or late filing of Form 2257 may give rise to a penalty of 5% of the underlying transactions, subject to statutory minimums.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (French domestic dividend withholding tax under Article 119 bis CGI) for dividends distributed to non-resident legal entities and individuals; treaty rates often reduce to 15%, 5%, or 0%. An EU/EEA parent company holding directly or indirectly at least 5% of the capital of the SAS for a continuous two-year period may qualify for a 0% withholding exemption under the French Parent-Subsidiary Directive implementation (Article 119 ter CGI).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA or EU-directive relief, the beneficial owner must: (i) obtain a valid tax-residence certificate from its own competent authority; (ii) complete and submit the French claim documentation (commonly via the Form 5000/2067 series and a formal shareholding attestation) to the French paying agent or the local tax office; (iii) prove the relevant ownership percentage, holding period, and absence of abuse under the Limitation-on-Benefits/Primary-Purpose-Test provisions; (iv) file any supporting declarations for the EU/EEA parent status. The reduced rate may be applied at payment only when a complete, valid claim is lodged before the withholding date; otherwise the standard 25% rate is collected and restitution can be sought through the French refund procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: French domestic statutory withholding is 33.33% (CGI Article 240/business licence jurisprudence) on patent, know-how and trademark royalties paid to non-residents; treaty rates commonly range from nil to 10%; the EU Interest and Royalties Directive reduces the rate to 0% for associated EU/EEA enterprises holding at least 25% direct capital for two years. Interest: France does not impose a general withholding tax on ordinary arm's-length commercial loan interest paid to non-residents; however, interest on certain debt securities or payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions may be subject to a special levy up to 50% (Article 125-0A CGI). Treaty rates for interest are frequently 0%, 5% or 10% depending on the beneficiary.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 (full Local File and Master File obligations are triggered when the French-domiciled entity or the consolidated group to which it belongs has annual consolidated turnover or balance-sheet total exceeding EUR 400,000,000); simultaneously, any SAS with related-party flows exceeding EUR 1,000,000 is subject to simplified French form 2257 intercompany declaration
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no separate Economic Substance Regulations comparable to offshore financial centres, but French abus-de-droit doctrine (Article L64 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales) plus DTA anti-abuse clauses impose a substance-over-form test. A DG forwarding SAS must maintain genuine operational substance: licensed dangerous-goods staff (IATA/IMDG-certified), physical offices or warehouses, insurance, fixed assets, bank accounts, invoices and contracts; otherwise treaty benefits may be denied and the entity recharacterised as a sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Designed concealment of taxable profits in the dangerous-goods forwarding business, use of fictitious invoices, cash-underreporting operation, or transfer of latent income to offshore shell accounts while continuing to control the SAS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil: penalty of 10% up to 80% of the evaded tax plus monthly late interest of 0.20%. Criminal (CGI Article 1741): up to three years' imprisonment and EUR 45,000 fine; aggravated offence (offshore concealment or organised fraud) rises to seven years and up to EUR 250,000 fine, publicity judgment, and asset confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors risk criminal conviction and imprisonment, travel bans, prohibition from commercial activity for up to ten years, personal collection of unpaid taxes and penalties, and civil liability to the company for any resultant loss or insolvency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Arrangement / Shell Company (Abus de droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating or operating the SAS as a pure letterbox with no physical presence, no DG licence substance, no real logistics operations, and interposed solely to obtain treaty benefits or avoid French corporate taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative reassessment of profits to the actual non-resident operator; 80% penalty under Article L64 LPFP plus late interest; denial of treaty benefits and, where applicable, reclassification of payments as constructive dividends subject to 25% withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers are jointly liable for reassessed taxes and penalties; the corporate veil may be pierced, leading to collection over personal assets, commercial disqualification, and criminal sanctions if intent is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, beneficial-owner identification, and suspicious-transaction reporting to TRACFIN; accepting cash payments above EUR 10,000 without proper declaration; involvement in sanctioned or illicit cargo movements through the DG forwarding channel.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative: suspension or revocation of the DG forwarding licence, fines up to EUR 2,000,000 under ACPR/DO orders. Criminal: money-laundering offences under the Monetary and Financial Code are punishable by up to five years' imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine; aggravated cases rise to ten years and EUR 20,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally subject to criminal imprisonment, fines, asset freezes, travel bans, and professional disqualification; they may also face tort liability for sanctions violations and damage to third parties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare, retain, or produce the Local File, Master File, or Form 2257 declaration in a timely manner; submission of incomplete, fabricated, or manifestly non-arm's-length documentation covering management fees, royalties, or intergroup financing flows in the DG operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 1735 bis CGI, a penalty equal to 5% of the amount of undisclosed or undocumentable intercompany transactions, with no statutory amnesty; additional ordinary reassessment plus late interest; penalty can reach 40%-80% in cases of deliberate or abusive manipulation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If directors knowingly caused or tolerated the defect, French courts may hold them personally liable for the penalty under management-fault (faute de gestion) doctrine, and criminal exposure arises where false documents are presented to the tax authority.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful Dividend Repatriation / Improper Treaty Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Disguising actual profit distributions as deductible interest, management fees, or inflated DG freight sub-charges to avoid French dividend withholding; fraudulently claiming a reduced treaty rate without satisfying the beneficial-owner, holding-period, and limitation-on-benefits conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation as a dividend subject to the full 25% French withholding tax, plus interest and a 40% penalty for bad faith; if the covered payment is a royalty reclassified with intentional concealment, an 80% abuse-of-law penalty can apply; criminal fraud sanctions are available.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or approved the misclassification may be jointly required to remit the unpaid withholding taxes with penalties; criminal conviction can add imprisonment, travel bans, and judicial liquidation of personal assets.
